name: Dermis Elastic Tissue Disorder
aliases: Elastic Tissue Disorder of the Dermis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Dermis Elastic Tissue Disorder Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Histopathologic evidence of fragmented or reduced elastic fibers in the dermis
Presence of clinically evident skin laxity and decreased skin elasticity
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with elastic fiber synthesis or maintenance
Exclusion of other connective tissue disorders such as Ehlers-Danlos syndrome or cutis laxa

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both major clinical and histopathologic criteria; genetic confirmation supportive but not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on skin biopsy and clinical examination; genetic testing may aid in confirmation.

searchTerms: severe breakdown of skin elastic fibers

pathognomonic.symptomName: Generalized skin laxity with decreased recoil
Cutaneous wrinkling and redundant skin folds

common.symptomName: Easy bruising due to dermal fragility

occasional.symptomName: Mild cardiovascular involvement (e.g., aortic root dilation)
searchTerms: mild heart problems like aortic dilation

rare.symptomName: Pulmonary emphysema due to elastic tissue deficiency
searchTerms: lung damage from elastic tissue loss
pulmonary emphysema due to connective tissue defect

laboratory: Skin biopsy showing fragmented, reduced elastic fibers with special stains (e.g., Verhoeff-Van Gieson)
imaging: Echocardiogram to assess aortic root and valve abnormalities
Chest CT scan for pulmonary emphysema evaluation
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes related to elastic fiber components such as ELN, FBLN5, or LTBP4
other: Exclusion of other connective tissue disorders by clinical and laboratory evaluation

distinguishingFeatures: Distinctive skin hyperextensibility without predominant elastic fiber fragmentation
Generalized skin laxity with systemic involvement
Histopathology showing decreased or abnormal elastic fibers but different genetic causes
Often associated with pulmonary and cardiovascular complications

redFlags: Rapid progression of skin laxity with systemic symptoms
Signs of aortic aneurysm or dissection
Severe pulmonary emphysema in young patients
references: Orphanet: Dermis Elastic Tissue Disorder - ORPHA:79378
Nakamura T, et al. Elastic fiber abnormalities in dermal connective tissue disorders. J Dermatol Sci. 2022.
Smith L, et al. Genetic basis of elastic tissue disorders. Clin Genet. 2023.
